scheme_name: PMMSY: Construction of  Plant/Storage of Minimum 30 Tonne Capacity - Gujarat
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India on May 20, 2020. 

This scheme aims to bring about a significant transformation in the fisheries sector. 

The PMMSY is designed to enhance fish production and productivity in India. 

The scheme is particularly focused on increasing the income of fishers and fish farmers. 

It also aims to create a sustainable and responsible fisheries sector. 

The PMMSY has a total outlay of ₹20,050 crores. 

This financial allocation is spread over a period from 2020 to 2025. 

The scheme is implemented in a mission mode to achieve its objectives effectively. 

One of the key components of PMMSY is the construction of fish storage and processing facilities. 

In Gujarat, the PMMSY specifically promotes the construction of plant/storage facilities with a minimum capacity of 30 tonnes. 

The objective of this initiative is to enhance the post-harvest management of fish. 

This includes improving the quality and shelf life of fish products. 

The scheme aims to increase the availability of fish in the market. 

It also seeks to reduce post-harvest losses which currently stand at around 20 to 30 percent. 

The benefits of this initiative include financial assistance for the construction of storage facilities. 

Eligible beneficiaries can receive up to 40 percent of the project cost as a subsidy. 

For Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, this subsidy can go up to 60 percent. 

The maximum subsidy amount for a storage facility under this scheme can be ₹1 crore. 

The eligibility criteria for availing benefits under this scheme include being a registered fish farmer or fisher. 

Applicants must be residents of Gujarat and must have a valid Aadhaar number. 

The age limit for applicants is generally set at 18 years and above. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required to apply for this scheme. 

The application process involves several steps to ensure transparency and efficiency. 

Interested beneficiaries must first visit the official website of the Fisheries Department of Gujarat. 

They need to download the application form available on the website. 

The completed application form must be submitted to the local fisheries office. 

Along with the application form, applicants must provide certain documents. 

These documents include proof of identity such as an Aadhaar card. 

Proof of residence is also required, which can be a utility bill or a ration card. 

Additionally, applicants must submit a project report detailing the proposed storage facility. 

The project report should include the estimated cost and the expected benefits. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the local fisheries office. 

The review process typically takes about 15 to 30 days. 

If approved, the applicant will receive a sanction letter detailing the subsidy amount. 

The disbursement of the subsidy is usually made in two installments. 

The first installment is released after the completion of the construction of the facility. 

The second installment is released after the facility becomes operational. 

The timeline for the entire process from application to disbursement can take up to six months. 

The implementing authority for this scheme in Gujarat is the Fisheries Department. 

The department operates under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

For any queries or assistance, beneficiaries can contact the Fisheries Department of Gujarat. 

The contact details can be found on the official website of the department. 

The PMMSY also aims to promote the use of modern technology in fish storage and processing. 

This includes the use of cold storage facilities to maintain the quality of fish. 

The scheme encourages the establishment of integrated fish processing units. 

These units are expected to create employment opportunities in the fisheries sector. 

The PMMSY is also aligned with the goal of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The scheme aims to increase fish production from 13.4 million tonnes in 2019-20 to 22 million tonnes by 2024-25. 

This translates to an annual growth rate of approximately 10 percent. 

The PMMSY is expected to benefit around 28 lakh fishers and fish farmers across India. 

In Gujarat, the scheme is particularly significant due to the state's extensive coastline. 

Gujarat has a coastline of approximately 1,600 kilometers. 

The state is known for its rich marine biodiversity and fishing culture. 

The PMMSY aims to harness this potential to boost the local economy. 

The scheme also emphasizes sustainable fishing practices. 

This includes promoting responsible fishing to protect marine ecosystems. 

The PMMSY is part of the larger Blue Revolution initiative. 

The Blue Revolution aims to increase fish production and improve the livelihoods of fishers. 

The PMMSY also focuses on enhancing the value chain in the fisheries sector. 

This includes improving infrastructure for fish marketing and distribution. 

The scheme encourages the establishment of fish markets and auction centers. 

These initiatives are expected to enhance the income of fishers significantly. 

The PMMSY is a comprehensive approach to developing the fisheries sector in India. 

It aims to create a robust framework for sustainable fish production and processing. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to the welfare of fishers. 

It seeks to empower them through financial assistance and infrastructure development. 

The PMMSY is a crucial step towards achieving self-sufficiency in fish production. 

It aims to make India a global leader in the fisheries sector. 

The scheme is expected to play a vital role in achieving food security in the country. 

The PMMSY is a significant initiative that reflects the government's vision for the fisheries sector. 

It aims to create a sustainable and prosperous future for fishers and fish farmers in India.
